findings.title: Critical security vulnerability affects OpenSSH on Alpine Linux systems | TLDR
findings.summary_md: TLDR reported on November 5, 2026 that OpenSSH 10.6p2 was released with a workaround for a critical vulnerability affecting Linux systems that use musl libc with PAM disabled, such as Alpine Linux. OpenSSH developer Damien Miller advised administrators of affected systems to immediately set PasswordAuthentication=no or disable SSH entirely.

findings.title: OpenSSH 10.6p2 Fixes Password Bypass on Alpine Linux
findings.summary_md: Privacy Affairs reported that OpenSSH 10.6p2 was released on November 5, 2026 with an emergency workaround for a critical flaw in sshd. On Linux systems built on the musl C library where sshd checks passwords itself instead of through PAM, accounts that should never accept a password will accept any password longer than 256 characters.

findings.title: OpenSSH and Alpine Linux warn of severe but niche bug | heise online
findings.summary_md: Heise Online reported that OpenSSH and Alpine Linux warned of a severe but niche authentication-bypass bug. OpenSSH developer Damien Miller warned users of affected systems to disable password-based login immediately via PasswordAuthentication=no and restart sshd, or disable SSH altogether. The flaw affects Linux systems using the musl C standard library without PAM.
